nav.feed: Ready-made post suggestions: skim and take into work
nav.events: All detected events with filters — the main workspace
nav.articles: Individual articles from sources, before grouping into events
nav.analytics: How many useful stories the team finds and how fast
nav.admin: Sources, dictionaries, settings, users and channels
nav.autopost: Automatic Telegram posting: switch, schedule and the channel as subscribers see it

language: Interface language. Article texts stay in the original language

filter.sport: Show events only for the selected sports
filter.competition: Show events only for the selected competitions
filter.relevance: How significant the news is for the channel. Based on keywords, teams and competitions
filter.trust: How reliable the reporting sites are: their trust level and how many are independent of each other
filter.source: Click to show only events with this source. Click again to exclude it: events with no other sources are hidden. A third click clears it
filter.status: Where the event is in the editorial workflow
filter.period: By the time of the latest article in the event
filter.conflicts: Sources contradict each other (e.g. different score) — needs checking
filter.region: Country of the sources. News from different countries is never merged into one event

relevance.MEDIUM: Notable news: publish if there is room
relevance.IRRELEVANT: Off-topic for the channel — most likely not sport
relevance.threshold_high: Points an article needs to be High. Higher — fewer high-importance events.
relevance.threshold_medium: From how many points an article is Medium. Below — Low.
relevance.body_weight: How much weaker a word found only in the text is than in the headline. 0 — text ignored, 1 — like the headline without doubling.
relevance.top_team_bonus: Added when the article mentions a club with the top priority (2) in Directories.
relevance.rumor_penalty: Subtracted when the text has rumor markers from the list below.
relevance.clickbait_penalty: Subtracted for a clickbait headline: “you won't believe…”, “!!” and their equivalents in the source language.
relevance.rules: News topic → weight. A negative weight lowers importance (e.g. sponsorship). The name is in the interface language; the words are in the language of the sources they are searched in: a Portuguese article is found only by Portuguese words. Whole words, ignoring case and accents; list word forms separated by commas.
relevance.competitions: Normally a competition adds its priority from Directories. Here you can give a specific competition another weight — name as in the directory.
relevance.rumor_markers: Phrases that mark an article as a rumor: “reportedly”, “according to sources” — in the source language.
relevance.check: Paste a headline (and the lead, if any) to see the points and where they come from. Uses the rules on this screen, even unsaved: change weights and see the effect.

trust.HIGH: Confirmed officially or by several independent reliable sources
trust.MEDIUM: One reliable source or several average ones
trust.LOW: Only weak sources or rumor signs — double-check
trust.UNKNOWN: Nothing to assess yet: sources have no trust level

status.NEW: Just detected, nobody has looked yet
status.REVIEWING: An editor is reviewing the event
status.SELECTED: Selected for publishing, post not written yet
status.READY: The post is approved and ready to publish
status.PUBLISHED: The post is out in the channel
status.REJECTED: Will not be published: duplicate, off-topic, error

badge.relevance: Relevance: how significant the news is for the channel
badge.trust: Source trust: how reliable the reporting sites are
badge.sources: How many sites reported it. Filled square: independent outlet; outlined: same media group as another one

tier.OFFICIAL: Official: club, league or federation site
tier.B: Tier B: reliable but less authoritative media
tier.UNTRUSTED: Untrusted: the source is collected but never confirms the news or counts as independent

event.summary: Short summary across all sources. Numbers [1] link to the source
event.why: Why the system rates the news this way: which words and entities scored
event.trust: How far the news can be trusted, based on who reported it
event.sources: Articles grouped into this event, in the original language
event.related: Similar events: follow-ups or possible duplicates
event.draft: Telegram post text: build it automatically or write your own
event.edit: Fix the title, summary, sport, teams
event.merge: Same event as another one? Merge their sources into one
event.brief: A short AI digest of the event in the chosen language: what happened, how confirmed it is, who is affected and what to do. Facts come only from the event's sources
event.brief_lang: Language the AI writes the brief in. Original articles are in the sources block above
event.brief_generate: Ask the AI to write a brief in the chosen language
event.brief_regenerate: Write the brief again — e.g. after new articles
event.brief_affected: Clubs, players and others affected by the news
event.brief_impact: What it means for the match, the team or the betting market
event.brief_actions: What to do or watch next
event.brief_sources: Articles the brief relies on. Links come from the event — the AI cannot invent them

workflow.REVIEWING: Take the event so colleagues see you are on it
workflow.READY: Approve the post: it is ready to publish
workflow.PUBLISHED: Mark that the post is already out in the channel
workflow.REJECTED: Do not publish. The reason feeds the statistics

draft.template: Build the text from the title and summary using a template — instant, editable afterwards
draft.regenerate: Rebuild the text. The current version stays in history
draft.history: All saved versions of the post: who changed it and when
draft.copy: Copy the post with formatting to paste into Telegram
draft.image: Image link. With an image the text limit is 1024 characters instead of 4096
draft.disclaimer: Verification status: the news is unconfirmed or sources conflict. Visible to the editorial team only — it is never added to the Telegram post; publishing is your call
draft.preview: How the post will look in the channel
draft.lang: Language of the current post version. Edits keep this language
draft.from_brief: Build a new post version from the AI brief in the chosen language. You can edit it; earlier versions stay in history
draft.ai: The AI writes a short post (headline and 2–3 sentences) from the event's sources in the interface language. You can edit it afterwards
draft.translate: Translate the draft — a new version appears; the previous one stays in history. The same text is translated only once
draft.channel_target: Only the current version goes to the channel, and only after the “Ready” status. Any new version — an edit, regeneration or translation — removes “Ready”: approve it again
draft.approve: The post is good as is: the event becomes “Ready” right away (even a new one — no intermediate steps) and goes to the channel on schedule

feed.suggested: Fresh important events with a ready post: approve, schedule or open for edits
feed.channel: Approved and published posts — as subscribers see them
feed.publish: Mark the post as published in the channel
feed.prepare: The first version is created automatically. This button writes it now: the AI in the editorial format and the channel language (without AI — from the template)
feed.rewrite: If the first version did not work out: write the post again, the previous one stays in the version history
feed.schedule: Approve the post (“Ready”) and put it in the channel calendar at the chosen time — in one step
feed.edit: Open the event: edit the post, sources and assessments
feed.approve: The post is good as is: status “Ready”, it goes to the channel on its schedule. Use “Schedule” to pick a time

source.tier: How much to trust the site. Feeds “Source trust”: official and major media confirm news, “Untrusted” never does
source.owner_group: Owner media group. Sites of one group do not count as independent confirmations
source.kind: Where articles come from. Below the list: what the selected type needs and an example address
source.parser_profile: How the feed and article text are read. The list depends on the source type
source.poll: How often to check the source for new articles
source.gap: Pause between requests to the same site so we do not overload it
source.ttl: After how many days to delete full article texts
source.test: Fetch the feed now and show what is found — without saving anything
source.health: ok — recent checks succeeded; degraded — some errors; down — the site does not respond
source.active: A disabled source is not checked; existing articles stay
source.region: Source country, 2-letter ISO code (RU — Russia, BR — Brazil; ZZ — worldwide, for international sources). Events never mix countries
source.tier_inline: The new trust level applies to articles collected after the change

pipeline.lag: Minutes from an article appearing on the site to the event in the system (for 95% of articles)
pipeline.queues: Background jobs: fetching, tagging, grouping. If jobs pile up, processing lags
pipeline.failed: Articles and jobs that failed. You can retry them

taxonomy.entities: Dictionary of teams, players and competitions. The system uses it to recognize them in text
taxonomy.aliases: Other spellings: abbreviations, nicknames. Avoid common words — they cause false matches
taxonomy.priority: The higher, the more relevance points a mention gives
taxonomy.unlinked: Names the system saw but could not find in the dictionary. Link or add them
taxonomy.display_name: How the competition is named in the interface and in hashtags of English posts. Empty — the source name is shown. Matching in articles is unaffected: it uses the source name and aliases.

analytics.useful: Events selected for work and not rejected as duplicate or error
analytics.hours: Active working time in the system (pauses under 15 min keep the session)
analytics.usph: Useful stories per hour — the main productivity metric
analytics.tts: Time from an event appearing to the decision to take it
analytics.precision: Share of “High relevance” events that actually went into work
analytics.edit_ratio: How heavily editors rewrite automatic drafts
analytics.leaders: Which sources most often report news first
analytics.ai_load: Whether the local model keeps up with the event flow. Each important event costs the AI a post (~a minute) and a translation; more sources mean more events. If it can't keep up, the queue grows and posts reach the Feed late. Below is what to change.
analytics.ai_share: How much of the day the AI needs for posts, translations and briefs at the current event flow and settings. Up to 50% is calm; above 85% the queue never clears.
analytics.ai_apply: Changes one setting for the whole newsroom right away. You can undo it in Admin → Settings.

settings.text: Plain-language description of what news matters. Used by AI only
settings.name: Short rule name — shown in “Why does it matter?”
settings.keywords: Words and phrases in the sources' language; whole-word match, case and accents ignored
settings.weight: Points the rule gives: ×2 in the title, scaled by “Article text weight” in the body. Negative lowers relevance
settings.LOW: Below this a sports item still gets “Low”
settings.sport_url_patterns: If the article URL contains a fragment (e.g. /football/), the sport is set immediately
settings.sport_keywords: Words that point to a sport. One word is not enough — a second signal is required
settings.ambiguous_entities: Clubs whose name is also a city or a common word (São Paulo, Internacional). Alone they do not make news sporty
settings.sports_domains: Domains where every item is sport (e.g. ge.globo.com). There ambiguous names count as clubs
settings.relevance_rules: Topics that make news more important: injuries, suspensions, coach changes…
settings.competition_weight: Extra points per competition. Default — the competition priority from the dictionary
settings.body_weight: How much matches in the article body count: 1 — like the title without doubling, 0.5 — half, 0 — title only
settings.rumor_markers: Phrases like “reportedly”, “according to sources” — in the source language. They lower importance and trust
settings.version: Increase when changing rules — shows which version tagged an article
settings.analysis_language: Language the AI uses for summaries and explanations
settings.telegram_language: Telegram draft language when a channel has none set
settings.enrich_article: Rules — free and instant; AI model — more accurate but slower
settings.cluster_adjudicate: Who decides when it is unclear whether it is one event: rules or AI
settings.event_summary: How to build the summary: from the main article's first paragraph (rules) or with AI
settings.telegram_draft: template — from a template, llm — written by AI
settings.conflict_check: Whether AI checks that sources do not contradict each other
settings.embeddings: Compare news by meaning, not just by words (needs a meaning-comparison model)
settings.llm_model: Model name at the provider, e.g. qwen3:14b
settings.escalation_model: A stronger model for hard cases. Empty — do not use
settings.error_rate: If the AI fails more often than this share (0.2 = 20%), fall back to rules
settings.window_minutes: Period over which errors are counted
settings.min_calls: Do not judge until there are at least this many calls
settings.pause_minutes: How long to run on rules after failures
settings.window_hours: A news item is compared with events from the last N hours
settings.top_k: How many similar events to check per news item
settings.w_cos: How much meaning similarity counts (with vectors on)
settings.w_entities: How much shared teams, players, coaches count
settings.w_competition: How much the same competition counts
settings.w_lex: How much shared words in headlines count
settings.lex_min: Below this share of shared words items are not grouped
settings.claim_conflict_penalty: How much to lower similarity when facts differ (different score)
settings.t_high: Similarity above this — the item joins the event right away. Lower — fewer splits, more wrong merges
settings.t_low: Similarity below this — a new event is created. Between thresholds rules or AI decide
settings.adjudication_enabled: Run an extra check for items between thresholds
settings.stale_similarity: How similar an old item must be to flag the new one
settings.trigram_threshold: How closely text spelling must match the dictionary name (0–1)
settings.auto_create_players: Unknown player names go to the dictionary for review
settings.min_relevance: Summaries are built only for events at this relevance or higher
settings.debounce_minutes: Rebuild the summary at most once per N minutes
settings.max_evidence_fragments: How many source quotes to pass to the AI
settings.max_text_chars_for_ai: How many article characters to send to the AI
settings.lead_max_chars: How many characters of the first paragraph to keep
settings.queue_age_minutes: Alert if a queued job waits longer
settings.ingest_lag_p95_minutes: Alert if articles take longer to process
settings.silent_source_hours: Alert if a source gives no new articles during working hours
settings.active_hours_start: At night silent sources are not a failure
settings.fetch_fail_streak: Alert if a source fails this many times in a row
settings.ai_error_rate: Alert if the AI fails more often
settings.repeat_minutes: How often to remind about an open problem
settings.channel_examples: Up to 5 style samples — the AI follows them
settings.include_source_link: Add a link to the original source in the post
settings.auto_min_relevance: Automatic processing (draft or AI brief) only for events at this relevance or higher
settings.sport_emoji: Emoji at the start of a post for each sport
settings.template_also_reported: Add other sources to the template post
settings.auto_languages: Languages to prepare briefs for automatically. The local model takes ~50 s per brief: 100 events ≈ 1.5 h per language
settings.max_age_hours: Only events with new articles in the last N hours
settings.ui_language: Interface language for all users. The AI translates titles and summaries of new events into it
settings.translate_min_relevance: Headlines are translated for every event. Summary and article leads — only from this importance (and for an opened event): several AI calls per event.
settings.translation_model: Local Ollama model for translations into the interface language.
settings.words: Words are searched in article texts, so they are in the source language: Portuguese for Brazilian sites, English and Russian for their own.

brief_status.official: Announced by the club, league or federation
brief_status.confirmed: Several reliable outlets report it as fact
brief_status.reported: Only one outlet reports it so far
brief_status.rumor: Speculation — do not publish as fact

channels.page: Where and on what schedule the system posts. The bot token lives in .env; here — only the channel address and rules
channels.name: How you will tell this channel apart in the list
channels.tg_chat_id: Channel ID like -100… (step 4 of docs/TELEGRAM_BOT_SETUP.md) or @username of a public channel
channels.language: Post language. “After approval” needs a post in this language; “Automatic” needs an AI brief in this language
channels.mode_approval: Only “Ready” events with a post in the channel language are published. After sending, the event becomes “Published”
channels.mode_auto: Events above the thresholds are published without a human; text is the AI brief in the channel language. Rumors are never published
channels.cron: How often to check for new events. Time is UTC (Moscow = UTC+3, Brasília = UTC−3)
channels.format: “One post per event” — separate messages; “Digest” — one message with a list of headlines and links
channels.max_per_run: Maximum events per run so the channel is not flooded
channels.min_relevance: Events below this relevance are not posted
channels.min_trust: Automatic mode only: how reliable the event's sources are
channels.min_tier: Posted only if at least one source is at or above this tier
channels.source_allow: If set, the event must include an article from at least one of them
channels.source_deny: Events with an article from these sources are not posted
channels.active: An inactive channel does not post on schedule; settings are kept
channels.test: Sends a real message to the channel — subscribers will see it. “Check” is usually enough. Click twice to confirm
channels.run: Post matching events right now without waiting for the schedule. Posts with a pinned time are left alone — they have their own time; to send one right away, use the button next to it
channels.check: Check the connection without posting anything: the bot sees the channel and may post

account: Your account: interface language, theme, sign out

block.independent: Independent outlet: its own media group. Click to jump to its article
block.same_group: Same media group as an outlet already counted: it does not add confirmation. Click to jump to its article

autopost.page: Automatic posting to Telegram channels: turn the switch on and the system sends matching posts on schedule. On the right — the channel as subscribers see it, plus scheduled posts
autopost.switch: Main switch of the channel. Off — nothing is sent on schedule or at pinned times, settings are kept. “Check”, “Test message”, “Run now” and “Send now” work even when it is off
autopost.journal: Every send: when, which event, success or the Telegram error
autopost.calendar: The week by hour in the time zone from your profile — change it there. Blue — goes out on schedule, yellow — time pinned by hand, red — time missed. Dashed top of a cell — a scheduled run, hatching — past time, red line — now. Drag a post into a cell: top half — :00, bottom half — :30
autopost.phone: A public channel is read from t.me (even when connected by a numeric -100… id), so manual posts are visible too. For a private channel it shows what the system sent. Dashed at the bottom — the posts that go out next
autopost.ready: Posts the channel is ready to send. Drag one onto the calendar and it goes out as a separate message at exactly that time instead of the next run. With the keyboard — enter the date and time in the field. Turning autoposting off stops pinned posts too
autopost.chip_auto: Goes out on schedule: {when}. Drag to pin another time
autopost.chip_missed: The time passed while autoposting was off, so it will not go out by itself. Drag it to a new time
autopost.unpin: Return the post to the regular scheduled queue
autopost.send_now: Publish this post right away, ignoring the schedule and the pinned time. Click twice to confirm

palette: Accent colour of the interface and logo: buttons, selection, links. Saved in this browser.

source_state.on: Click again to exclude this source

post_format.title: Shared rules for every post: what to include and the example the AI follows when writing new posts
post_format.include_emoji: ⚽, 🏀 etc. before the headline, by the event’s sport
post_format.inline_links: The AI links phrases in the text, as in the example (“reported by ge”). Addresses come only from the event’s sources
post_format.include_source_link: A separate line with the main source name and its link
post_format.template_also_reported: Template posts only: a line with other outlets that covered the event
post_format.hashtags: Up to 4 hashtags: the event’s competition and teams
post_format.example: A finished post as it should look: length, paragraphs, bold, links in the text. The AI copies the form, not the facts. Links may point anywhere — in a new post they are replaced with the event’s sources
post_format.use_current: Make the text in the editor above the example
post_format.instructions: Free-form instructions for the AI: length, tone, what to mention
post_format.auto_mode: On — for every important event the AI writes the post in this format in the channel language, one at a time, important first; progress shows in the Feed. Off — the template right away, AI only on Rewrite. Turn it off if the AI can't keep up (see Analytics → AI load).

ai.queue: What the AI is doing right now and how long the queues will take. There is one model and it works in turn: important and fresh events first. Times come from recent measurements; if the queue does not shrink, see Analytics → AI load.

tz.mismatch: The device time zone comes from the computer's system clock, not from the IP address, so a VPN does not affect it. If you are somewhere other than your profile says, switch — the calendar, feed and posting times will show your local time.
tz.select: All dates and times in the app are shown in this zone, and posting times are picked in it. The server stores UTC, so changing the zone moves nothing — only the display changes.

list.translating: The headline is still in the source language: the AI is translating it, usually within a minute or two. Progress is in the Feed and Analytics.
